content.title: About
content.content: Gruyère is a Swiss semi-hard cheese with a nutty, slightly sweet flavor and characteristic "eyes". Made from cow’s milk in the Fribourg‑Vaud region, it is aged from 6 to 24 months. The cheese has a dense, slightly grainy texture and an aroma that deepens with age.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Gruyère takes its name from the Swiss town of Gruyères, where production began in the 12th century.
Traditional aging involves regular turning and cleaning of the rind.
The cheese is a staple in fondue, raclette, and classic French dishes such as quiche.
There are more than 30 official varieties of Gruyère, each with a different aging period.
Gruyère holds a Protected Designation of Origin (AOP) status, guaranteeing its authenticity.

items.title: Rich in calcium
items.content: Calcium in Gruyère supports strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Good source of protein
items.content: The cheese provides high‑quality dairy protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Gruyère contains vitamin B12 and riboflavin, important for the nervous system and energy metabolism.

items.title: Healthy fats
items.content: In moderate amounts, the cheese contributes beneficial fatty acids to a balanced diet.

items.title: Probiotic bacteria
items.content: Fermentation introduces beneficial microbes that can support gut health.

items.title: Lactose
items.content: People with lactose intolerance may experience discomfort after consuming Gruyère.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: The cheese is relatively salty, so individuals with hypertension should limit portions.

items.title: Milk‑protein allergy
items.content: Some individuals may have an allergic reaction to casein.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Gruyère is calorie‑dense, so it should be eaten in moderation.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Gruyère is perfect grated over pasta, salads, casseroles, and sandwiches. It can be served in thin slices with fruit, nuts, or as part of a cheese board. For fondue, cut the cheese into cubes and melt slowly with white wine.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store Gruyère in its original packaging or wrapped in parchment paper inside an airtight container in the refrigerator at 2‑4 °C. For longer storage, wrap it in aluminum foil and keep it in a cool cellar. Before use, remove any dry rind.
